criteria.bounded_grants: Make authorization evidence explicit and portable: authorizing reads mint bounded grants naming operation, targets, versions, predicate outcome, checkpoint and expiry, and effects present them at commit for validation against versions, fence, expiry and revocation list. Display reads pass no grant and can never authorize; transitive effects mint their own non-transferable grants; spends require dispatch-claim-fresh grants. The read-to-effect gap is named exactly, with bounds, instead of fenced ambiently. Price: grant lifecycle, revocation retention, expiry basis (wall-clock against the fixed test clock, or revision distance), spanning diagnostics and projection support are all new specified surface; every commit consults the revocation list; and the customer is missing — fence or pins close the gap with far less, so this pays the most for auditability no workflow has requested while risking invisible inference or crushing annotation.
criteria.checkpoint_fence: Keep every workflow exactly where the drafts put it: one owner checkpoint per operation enrolls all guard, when, derive, policy and membership reads in the settled fence, and the fenced commit re-asserts the checkpoint plus revalidates permission and revocation against live authority state, failing closed on any intervening change. Chat spend, can_use, the Creative guard and the Check heartbeat all run inside one fence each with zero draft edits, and transitive hook and handler effects simply open fresh checkpoints of their own. Price: the revalidation pass doubles predicate evaluation on mutations; hot allowance rows and the membership table become conflict sources; each failure must attribute its invalidating read; the database-wide assertion couples unrelated operations to revocation bookkeeping until a narrower fence is proven acceptable.
criteria.pinned_snapshots: Give reads surgical freshness: each authorizing read pins its observed record versions and checkpoint, the commit rechecks pins plus live by and revocation, and only pinned records plus authority tables must be unchanged — an unrelated write elsewhere no longer voids the operation. Genuinely stale-tolerant views (cross-owner browsing, pickers, progress) take an explicit eventual label, pin nothing, and can never authorize or spend by static rule. Same-owner workflows stand unedited; the label applies only where eventual views exist, and none are sampled yet. Price: capture-and-assert pin machinery on every read; a second read kind with its own diagnostics and teaching; D1 narrowed-assertion semantics to prove or this collapses into the checkpoint rule carrying dead bookkeeping; and every future read litigates authorizing-versus-eventual with a pinned-safe default to defend.
criteria.read_at_effect: Refuse the snapshot problem instead of solving it: no predicate result crosses any boundary, each effect re-reads live authorization and state at claim time, dispatch and spend validations already work this way and simply generalize. Display reads keep their reread contract; transitive effects are trivially fenced as ordinary effects. Safety reasoning is local to each effect point with no carried state to track. Price: the drafts' read-guard-act shape is abandoned — Chat allowance code either silently re-reads through let bindings, contradicting the captured-value rule, or every multi-effect site is rewritten with re-queries and per-site proof burden; multi-effect operations multiply their authorization reads; and the revision fence stays anyway for write-write conflicts, so this keeps fence machinery, adds N effect reads, and still invites authors to recreate carried gaps through let.

read_rule.instructions: For the authoritative-read gate, which rule best preserves the six accepted workflows, keeps stale reads and mid-flight revocation from silently authorizing commits and spends, and minimizes semantic surface, migration churn and contention risk? Judge every option under the same workflow-preservation and minimal-intervention constraints.

state: Accepted workflows come first at this gate: Chat spend flows, can_use gating, the Creative guard and the Check heartbeat must each run with their reads fenced and their effects authorized, and six bar items pin that behavior with zero draft edits as the preservation standard. The corpus they live in holds 473 pure-position lines across 50 files spanning policy, derive, crud-when, send-when, lock-when, invariant and page classes, plus 288 spend effects (236 sends to 69 targets, 22 money creations, 27 allowance writes) traced from guard to effect. Revocation already bites live: Grant's deactivate-then-decide sequence denies immediately, so any rule must preserve that immediacy rather than invent it. The settled floor under all four options is the D1 database-wide optimistic fence with admission-time evaluation and commit-time permission recheck, atomic guard-plus-claim dispatch, mandate-validating payment collect, and reread/stale-marked display reads. Landed around the gate: T06 R26-layer-1 narrowing, complete T16 with state-side T17a and a verified T17b flip, T28-A same-owner fencing for imported-parent reads, and T31a flat hook staging. The open edges each option must survive: T29 imported atomicity still owed; zero draft examples executing an intra-operation gap (9 sequence candidates, 31 conflict rows, no active_member or mid-flight let observations, R29 alias flip open, T23/T22/T21 pending); fence evidence still plan-not-proof with memory limits and DECISIONS #138 open; active_member still barred from pure positions for lack of a bounded-read contract; no T24 dispatch record; D1 contention already the leading runtime uncertainty. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation result.
